races.title: State House, District 43
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Diane Wheatley
cands.bio: Registered nurse and small-business owner (government contract work with her husband). Served on the Cumberland County school board 1994–2004 and as county commissioner 2004–2008. Republican member of the NC House for District 43 from 2021; lost the November 2026 general election.

endorsements.text: The Civic Table (Sway voting group by Carrie Jackson) listed her in its 2026 voter guide recommendations, according to Ballotpedia.

cands.gaps: We could not find the year she moved to North Carolina or details of her childhood before high school. We found no stated positions or documented actions on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buying, growth and land conservation, immigration or H-1B, gun laws, or abortion. We found no documented controversies, foreign ties, or notable endorsements beyond one voter-guide listing. She did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in 2022, 2024 or 2026. Her 2020 survey answers cover background and general priorities only. The claim on her campaign site that she returned over $400 million to Cumberland County is self-reported and not independently verified.

local.label: Roots 80: She was born at Fort Campbell, Kentucky, attended high school in Fayetteville after her father's transfer to Fort Bragg, married a Fayetteville man in 1973, and has held local office in Cumberland County since 1994.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: NC House member for District 43 from 2021 to 2027 (serving on appropriations and education budget committees); Cumberland County school board member and twice chair (1994–2004); county commissioner (2004–2008); registered nurse; co-owner of a school bus and military transportation contracting business for over 30 years.
qual.why: She has several years of prior legislative service, a decade on a school board that oversaw a $98 million bond, and county commission experience. She also has business ownership and a nursing career. Committee posts were not counted.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: Her campaign site says she supports rewarding hard-working teachers and expanding educational options so families can choose the best school for their children.

back-police-order.evidence: Her campaign site calls her a strong and vocal supporter of law enforcement and school resource officers and says community safety is her top priority.

cands.name: Janene Ackles
cands.bio: Nonprofit consultant and grant writer who says she has worked with nonprofits, municipalities and community organizations for over 20 years. Ran for Fayetteville City Council in 2019 and lost, and for NC House District 43 in 2024 and lost. Won the District 43 seat in 2026, defeating incumbent Diane Wheatley.

endorsements.text: Progressive Caucus of the North Carolina Democratic Party, and the voter guides The Civic Table and Unburdening The Ballot, are listed as 2026 endorsements.
In her own Ballotpedia survey she lists endorsements from Cumberland County Democrats, State Senator Val Applewhite, the NCDP Progressive Caucus and Planned Parenthood (self-reported).

cands.gaps: We couldn't find where Ackles was born or raised, or when she moved to North Carolina. We found no record of her taking positions on data centers, development and growth, homestead property taxes, foreign or investor land buying, immigration or H-1B, policing, guns or abortion. The pages we could read did not show any actions she took in office. Her career details come only from her own survey answers and Ballotpedia's brief profile, and we could not confirm them independently.

score.why_money: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: She describes more than 20 years as a nonprofit consultant and grant writer, securing funding and building programs with nonprofits, municipalities and community groups. Ballotpedia lists her as a business consultant. She has held no elected office; she lost the 2019 Fayetteville City Council District 2 race and the 2024 House race.
qual.why: Her consulting and grant-writing work touches public funding and programs, which is somewhat relevant. She has no prior legislative or local elected service, and the work history comes from her own survey answers and is not independently verified.
